documentation.title: Coulomb friction: one interface, one sticking point and one slipping point
documentation.description:
Gate for a MIXED interface -- stick and slip coexisting -- and for the default friction tangent.
The ContactPatchTest2d geometry: two QUAD9 blocks with a coincident interface at y = 1, the lower body fixed at the bottom. The upper body has NO displacement boundary condition at all, so BOTH its supports run through the contact interface: the normal one through the penalty, the tangential one through friction. That is what makes the tangential number a statement about friction rather than about a reaction the solver would have produced anyway.
ContactFrictionStick2d with the tangential traction raised from 5e4 to 2e5 Pa, against mu = 0.4 and 1e6 Pa normal. Globally there is ample friction, but not where it is needed: the tangential traction acts a block height above the interface, so it carries a moment and the balancing pressure comes out linear in x. The windward point cannot hold an equal share, so it slips at exactly its limit and the leeward point sticks and takes the remainder.
numStickPoints = 1, numSlipPoints = 1 totalTangentialForce = p_T * L = 4e5 EXACT by equilibrium, though one point is capped totalContactForce = p_N * L = 2e6
The resultant is the strong check -- fixed by equilibrium whatever the split -- while the split itself is fixed by the Coulomb law and the pressure distribution.
IT ALSO GATES tangent="reduced" AS THE DEFAULT: with tangent="consistent" this model does not converge at all, because a slipping point has no tangential stiffness to balance the consistent normal-coupling term. Switching that one attribute reproduces the failure.
